conviction_note: This print turns on Deere's first FY2027 net income guide. Barchart's FY27 consensus is $23.40 EPS (about $6.3bn of net income at about 269m shares). Bernstein publicly expects a reset to $5.4bn / $20. Deere's last two first-year guides came in 12-16% below the street, and the stock went +8% (Nov 2024) and -5.7% (Nov 2025). Against that, the stock has already fallen about 9% from ~$673 to ~$617 in the week into the print, and the October data are improving: Deere's callbacks to build dealer inventory, CNH's positive MY27 order intake, AEM 4WD +7.7%, and used inventories down 15%. The findings net to about +0.1 and the scaled number to -0.24 (p_up 48, abs 6.0). The two disagree only marginally; both say the evidence balances around a guide that will likely sit under $23.40, against a stock that has partly priced that.

That sits inside the company's FY26 net income guide of $4.75-5.00bn, which implies Q4 net income of about $0.94-1.19bn, or roughly $3.50-4.40 EPS (https://finviz.com/news/383975/deere-reports-third-quarter-net-income-of-1379-billion, 2026-08-20). The bar that moves the stock is FY27 consensus: Barchart $23.40 EPS (+29%), MarketBeat $21.56 on four estimates, Bernstein $20 / $5.4bn, and Oppenheimer's survey of +20-25% EPS growth. The FY27 bar is disputed, so the guidance findings are capped at moderate size. The sweep row's FY26 guide of $4.00-4.75bn is stale; it was raised to $4.75-5.00bn on 2026-08-20.

next_guide.basis: Deere's first-year guides were about 12% (Nov 2024) and about 16% (Nov 2025) below the street midpoint. The FY27 tariff step-up (about +$250m) and the end of $382m of FY26 refunds are headwinds. Early orders up mid-single digits, CNH's positive MY27 intake and the October callbacks argue for a recovery guide. The expected direction is an initiation whose midpoint sits below $23.40, likely around $5.3-6.0bn.

findings.finding: Deere's first FY27 net income guide is likely to land below the street's FY27 bar. Barchart consensus is $23.40 EPS (+29%, about $6.3bn at about 269m shares). Bernstein publicly forecasts $5.4bn / $20 (5-10% below consensus), and Oppenheimer sees limited room to beat. Deere's previous two first-year guides were set well below the street: FY25 at $5.0-5.5bn (midpoint EPS about $19 against $21.58 consensus) and FY26 at $4.0-4.75bn against $5.19bn consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The first-year guide moved the stock both ways. On 2024-11-21 the FY25 guide was about 12% below the street but came with a large Q4 beat ($4.55 against $3.87), and the stock rose about 8% (Nasdaq/Citi, https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/citi-anticipates-deere-shares-react-positively-q4-beat). On 2025-11-26 the FY26 guide of $4.0-4.75bn was against $5.19bn consensus, and the stock fell 5.67% (sealed baseline; https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/why-deere-stock-dropped-today).
findings.why_not_priced: The headline consensus still reads $23.40 (Barchart, 2026-11-22). If the market had fully adopted Bernstein's $20, the published mean would be near $21 and mean targets would not sit 12-15% above spot. The 9% pre-print slide and the put skew show it is partly priced.
findings.independence: Bernstein's view and Oppenheimer's comment both come from TipRanks. Investing.com (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/deere-earnings-up-next-can-guidance-ease-downturn-fears-93CH-5048535, 2026-11-24) carries Bernstein independently. The Nov 2024 and Nov 2025 guide gaps come from separate sources (Nasdaq/Citi; Bloomberg/Nasdaq).

findings.finding: Deere's CFO said on the Aug 20 call that FY27 tariff expense will run at about $1bn against about $750m net in FY26, a step-up of about $250m pre-tax (about 4% of FY26 net income after tax). The $382m of FY26 tariff refunds ($272m Q2 + $110m Q3) will not recur, and no refund is assumed in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tariff costs ($1.2bn gross FY26) were cited in the Nov 2025 guide that sold off 5.7%. This line has not surprised on its own since.
findings.why_not_priced: It has been public since August and is partly in the models. The street's +29% FY27 EPS growth is hard to reconcile with a $250m cost step-up plus the loss of refunds, which suggests some estimates do not fully carry it. If they did, consensus would sit nearer Bernstein's $20.
findings.independence: The Q3 release (https://finviz.com/news/383975/deere-reports-third-quarter-net-income-of-1379-billion) confirms $110m / $382m of refunds. OptionBeast (2026-11-21) also says the refunds are unlikely to recur in FY27. Both rest on the same Aug 20 company statements.

findings.finding: Inside the quarter, Deere recalled all remaining laid-off workers at Waterloo, Ottumwa, Dubuque and the Quad Cities (more than 275 at Waterloo) and is hiring more than 400 at Illinois, Iowa and Kansas plants, including Harvester Works (combines) and Seeding. A spokesperson said on 2026-10-07 that this is to 'build dealer inventory ahead of upcoming planting and harvest cycles' and to serve customers 'including future labor negotiations'. That points to higher early-FY27 production and better absorption than FY26's deliberate underproduction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on a production-rate statement in the baseline window. In Aug 2026, early-order commentary was called 'the most significant' item by Raymond James, and the stock rose 6.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: It was covered as labor and local news, not in sell-side previews, none of which mention it. Part of the build is a hedge ahead of the UAW contract expiring 2027-10-31, which UAW members declined to extend on 2026-08-23. So it is partly a one-time pre-build, not demand. Sized net of that.
findings.independence: CNH reports positive MY27 order intake (finding 5). AEM October data show large tractors up (finding 7). The contract timing is from AgWeb/RTTNews (https://www.rttnews.com/3683707/uaw-members-reject-deere-contract-extension-offer.aspx).

findings.finding: On 2026-11-04 Deere announced it will close Ottumwa (windrowers and balers to Des Moines by 2027-2028) and end manufacturing at Hagie/Clarion (STS sprayers to Thibodaux by 2029). It said it is 'currently operating far below normal production volumes'. No charge was quantified; Q4 or FY27 restructuring charges are possible.
findings.why_not_priced: Any charge would be small against about $5bn of net income and is below the operating line. The 'far below normal volumes' quote is consistent with the known underproduction.

findings.finding: CNH (Q3, 2026-11-09) said North American order intake for MY27 is modestly positive against MY26 and the ag industry is 'approaching the end of this cyclical trough'. It cut ag dealer inventory by about $100m in Q3, with more in Q4. North American Q3 industry volume: tractors over 140 HP -5%, under 140 HP -12%, combines -13%. It also called the 2027 outlook 'uncertain'.
findings.link: CNH is Deere's closest same-product competitor in North American large ag (tractors over 140 HP, combines). It sells into the same dealer channel and growers. CNH ag sales were $2.9bn in the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: It came after Deere last spoke. Previews do not cite it. The FY27 consensus of +29% already assumes a recovery, so it supports the street rather than beats it.
findings.independence: The AEM October data (https://www.rfdtv.com/four-wheel-drive-tractor-sales-rise-despite-broader-equipment-weakness) point the same way for large tractors.

findings.finding: AGCO (Q3, 2026-10-29) cut its industry outlooks for Western Europe, Latin America and North America. Its CEO called it the weakest global industry demand in more than a decade. Net sales were -8.6%, but North America was +35% in constant currency.
findings.link: AGCO is a direct competitor in tractors and combines (Fendt, Massey Ferguson) in Europe, South America and North America. Its 2026 sales are about $9-10bn, against Deere's PPA and SAT exposure to the same regions.
findings.why_not_priced: AGCO's cut is public. Deere's own FY26 regional guides (US/Canada large ag and South America -15 to -20%, Europe flat) are already below. The relevance is FY27 Europe and South America, where Deere has not spoken.
findings.independence: Abimaq Brazil data (finding 10) agree on South America. The AGCO 8-K is at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000880266/000088026626000075/a2026earningsreleaseq3.htm.

findings.finding: AEM US data for October 2026 (Deere's fiscal Q4): 4WD tractors +7.7% y/y (337 against 313) and 100+ HP 2WD +3.2%, against YTD 4WD -19% and total tractors -11.6%. Combines -9.6% (YTD -9.1%). Large tractors turned positive in the last month of the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an industry unit proxy, widely available to ag analysts and not company-level. It is small, at 337 units.
findings.independence: Proxy. CNH's Q3 over-140 HP figure (-5%, a smaller decline than under 140 HP) is consistent.

findings.finding: Sandhills (September 2026): used tractor (100+ HP) inventory -14.82% y/y, down for 16 consecutive months, with auction values +4.8% y/y. Used combine inventory -9.51% with auction values +2.74% y/y, but combine values are trending down month to month.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Deere's CEO cited 'improved used inventories' as a bottoming signal on 2026-08-20, and the stock rose 6.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a proxy and public, consistent with management's August message. It supports a recovery guide rather than surprising.
findings.independence: OptionBeast (2026-11-21, https://wp.optionbeast.com/2026/11/21/deere-reports-tuesday-the-fy2027-guide-is-what-counts/) says North American high-horsepower tractor and combine inventory is more than 50% below the mid-2024 peak. Raymond James says dealer inventories are at multi-year lows (Investing.com 2026-11-24).

findings.finding: Purdue/CME Ag Economy Barometer, October 2026 (released 2026-11-03): headline 123 to 126. The Farm Capital Investment Index jumped from 39 to 55, its highest since December, helped by ARC/PLC government payments. Only 20% say it is a good time to buy machinery and buildings.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a public macro survey and a proxy. Its transmission to Deere's guide is unconfirmed.

findings.finding: Brazilian ag machinery industry revenue (Abimaq) was -15.7% y/y in September 2026 and -21.6% YTD through September. Abimaq expects about -20% for 2026, citing high rates and deferred investment. That is weak carry-over into Deere's FY27 South America.
findings.why_not_priced: Deere already guides South America -15 to -20% for FY26, so this is in line for FY26. The FY27 recovery assumption there is the open part.
findings.independence: CNH's Q3 reports South America tractors -22% and combines -19%.

findings.finding: Caterpillar's Q3 2026 (2026-10-29): sales +17%, Construction Industries profit +33% ($1.83bn), and 'strong order rates and a record backlog'. Construction demand supports Deere's C&F, which is guided +20% in FY26 and running at a 12.1% margin.
findings.link: Same end market and products (earthmoving and construction equipment, North American dealers). Deere C&F is about 30% of equipment operations sales (Q3: $3.62bn of $11.0bn).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 C&F +18% and +84% operating profit was the headline of the +6.9% August reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is widely known. CAT itself fell about 9.5% on its print, so construction strength is not a free pass.
findings.independence: CNH's construction outlook was raised to +8-10% and North American construction demand is +10%. Deere raised construction production rates per Manufacturing Dive (2026-11-02).

findings.finding: Expectations have reset in price. The stock fell from $673.54 to $609.25 (-9.5%) between about 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-20 and sits about $617 into the print (5-day -5.0%), 13% below its September all-time high. Bernstein's below-consensus 'reset' view is circulating. A guide that merely meets the lowered buy-side bar ($5.4-5.8bn) can be read as 'not as bad' rather than a miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2024: a below-street guide met a stock bought on Q4 quality, +8%. Nov 2025: a below-street guide, -5.7%. Neither run-up is in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: This runs against the options market (skew +14.5, downside paid). The case for it: the skew prices a guide below $23.40, and the buy-side has had a week and a public Bernstein note to move there. If the reset were fully priced, the slide would be smaller than 9% only if the guide were expected near consensus. The case is thin, so sized small.
findings.independence: OptionBeast close of $609.25 on 2026-11-20 (https://wp.optionbeast.com/2026/11/21/deere-reports-tuesday-the-fy2027-guide-is-what-counts/). The baseline's 5-day -5.0% shares the price-path fact.

findings.finding: The Q4 EPS bar ($4.01-4.07, about $1.09bn net income) sits in the upper half of the FY26-guide-implied Q4 range ($0.94-1.19bn). Deere beat in Q4 FY24 ($4.55 against $3.87), Q4 FY25 ($3.93 against $3.84) and Q3 FY26 ($5.10 against $4.69). The guide assumes no Q4 tariff refunds, so a recognised refund would be upside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 beats were followed by +8% (2024) and -5.7% (2025). The quarter did not decide either; the guide did.
findings.why_not_priced: A beat is the base case and is inside the company guide, so little of it is unpriced.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-20 Deere said MY27 sprayer and planter early-order programs were running up mid-single digits y/y and reiterated '2026 will mark the bottom of the current ag equipment cycle'. Raymond James called the early-order comments 'perhaps the most significant within the release'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August print rose 6.9% with this commentary.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced. What is new on Nov 25 is the completed MY27 EOP and the large-ag industry outlook, where a 'measured recovery' framing would disappoint a +29% EPS street.
findings.independence: Same company statement as the MarketBeat call summary. CNH's positive MY27 intake is independent (finding 5).

findings.finding: Raymond James ($730 target) says Deere's dealer inventories are at multi-year lows, while noting mixed sentiment on recent Corn Belt dealer visits. North American high-horsepower tractor and combine inventories are more than 50% below the mid-2024 peak.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a published sell-side view and mostly priced. Lean inventory means retail demand converts to production without destocking, which supports a higher production guide.
findings.independence: OptionBeast's '>50% below peak' figure (2026-11-21). Shares the theme with finding 8 (used inventory), which is a different series.

findings.finding: Short interest is about 2% of float with 4.1-4.6 days to cover and falling (Sept 30 settlement; ORTEX Oct 27). There is no crowded short and no squeeze mechanism.
findings.why_not_priced: Neutral: it neither amplifies nor dampens.

findings.finding: Investing.com reports Deere acquired Orchard AI on 2026-11-19. No terms or company release were found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tuck-in tech acquisitions (GUSS, Smart Apply) have not moved prints.
findings.independence: None found; a search for a Deere release returned nothing.

Ottumwa and Clarion footprint consolidation: savings and charges land 2027-2029.

baseline_tension: The main negative (a FY27 guide below the $23.40 street) agrees with the +14.5 put skew. The positive expectations finding runs against it on the argument that a 9% slide into the print has pre-paid part of the reset. The many small recovery proxies (CNH, AEM, used inventory, hiring) offset the guide risk, so the net is near zero and p_up sits just under 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (sign against a strong skew): the expectations finding, which is long against +14.5 put skew, went from +0.8 to +0.5. why_not_priced now states why the option market may be over-paying.

Lessons 1 and 6 (verified fact is not a reaction; inside the guide): the Q4 consensus-beat finding went from +0.4 to +0.2, because it lands inside the company's FY26 guide and the last two Q4 beats were followed by opposite moves.
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the hiring and callback finding went from +1.0 to +0.7, because part of the build is a hedge ahead of UAW negotiations rather than demand.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): the plant-closure finding went from -0.2 to -0.1 as a below-the-line item with no quantified charge.
Lesson 5 (proxies): the CAT peer finding went from +0.4 to +0.3. AEM, Sandhills, Purdue and Abimaq were already small and stay filed.
p_up moved from 49 to 48: the guide-gap lean agrees with the skew, and the low short interest gives no squeeze offset. abs_move_pct stays 6.0 (first FY guide, above the 4.72 event-implied move).
